t: The National Trust, a conservation organisation in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, was founded.
Oscar Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest, once described as the second-most quoted English-language play after Hamlet, premiered in London.
The libel trial instigated by Irish author Oscar Wilde began, eventually resulting in his arrest, trial and imprisonment on charges of gross indecency.
Backed by Samuel J. Tilden, the Astor Library and the Lenox Library agreed to merge and form the New York Public Library.
Oscar Wilde was sentenced by Alfred Wills to two years of hard labor for gross indecency.
The U.S. Court of Private Land Claims ruled that James Reavis's claim to 18,600 sq mi (48,000 km2) of land in present-day Arizona and New Mexico was "wholly fictitious and fraudulent".
At Gare Montparnasse in Paris, an express train derailed after overrunning the buffer stop and crashed through the station wall.
Swedish chemist and industrialist Alfred Nobel signed his last will and testament, setting aside the bulk of his estate to establish the Nobel Prize after his death.
The Chicago Times-Herald race, the first automobile race in the U.S., was held in Chicago.
